note: Retard means both delay and lateness; the latter is central in en retard = late.
The intransitive/reflexive idea 'be interested' is expressed with s'intéresser à; bare intéresser means interest/concern. The gloss should distinguish them.
proposed_english: to interest; to concern; to be interested in (s'intéresser à)

note: Clair is primarily clear/light/bright/pale. English 'clearly' is not a normal direct adjective gloss; adverbial uses are construction-dependent.
proposed_english: clear; light; bright; pale; open/clear area (noun use, context-dependent)

note: 'Back' is not a normal meaning of grave. Core learner senses are serious/severe/grave and low-pitched/deep.
Vivant also functions as a noun meaning a living person/being; noun POS is listed but the noun meaning is absent.
Libre should foreground free/available/vacant/unoccupied; 'freestyle' is a specialized use and should not lead the learner gloss.
proposed_english: free; at liberty; available; vacant; unoccupied; free/open

note: Baiser has a strong modern register split: as a noun it means kiss; as a verb it commonly means 'to fuck' (vulgar), while the older/literary verbal 'kiss' survives in limited use. This must be labeled to avoid a serious learner mistake.
proposed_english: kiss (noun); to fuck (verb, vulgar); to kiss (verb, older/literary)

note: Bare taire is transitive ('to keep quiet/conceal/not say'); the intransitive 'be quiet/fall silent' is se taire. The current gloss conflates them.
proposed_english: to keep quiet; to conceal; not to say; to be quiet/fall silent (se taire)
